subject: Money
title: How CPI Is Measured
description: One-minute skill: How CPI Is Measured.

hook.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics sends agents to 23,000 stores monthly to check prices on 80,000 items.

buildup.text: CPI tracks a fixed basket of goods: food, housing, healthcare, transport, education, recreation.

discovery.text: Each category is weighted by spending habits. Housing is 33% of CPI because Americans spend a third of income on it.

twist.text: Critics say CPI understates true inflation. It substitutes cheaper goods when prices rise—steak becomes hamburger.

climax.text: CPI affects Social Security, tax brackets, and wages for millions. Getting the number wrong costs billions.

quiz.question: Why do some critics say CPI understates inflation?
options: It substitutes cheaper goods when prices rise
